description: Puts two to five registry servers next to each other from the board's latest daily probe: status, how a client gets in, tool count, token cost (exact in Claude when counted, else the estimate), share of a 200k window and initialize latency, with the cheapest, the most expensive and the spread. Use it to choose between servers that do the same job; use lookup_server for the full record of one server, search_servers to find candidates, and check_server for a URL that is not in the registry. Instant, no connection to the servers. A name the board does not know gets a row with status "unknown" and the comparison goes on. format picks the text layout (JSON, a Markdown table, or CSV to paste into a spreadsheet); the structured content is always JSON.

format.description: The layout of the text content: json (default), markdown (a table with a summary line), or csv (a header row, then one row per server)

servers.description: Two to five registry names (io.github.owner/name) or the servers' https URLs as the registry lists them

name: compare_servers

cheapest.description: The server with the fewest tokens, when two or more rows are measured

measured.description: How many rows have a token number

servers.description: One row per requested server, in the order given

authKind.description: oauth-dcr, oauth, token or unknown, for a server that needs auth

error.description: Why there is no data, for example "not on the board"

exact.description: Whether tokens is the exact count

name.description: The registry name, or what was given when the board does not know it

page.description: The server's page on the board

status.description: The probe status, or "unknown" when the board has no such server

tokens.description: The number compared: the exact count when it exists, else the estimate

tokenSpread.description: Tokens between the most expensive and the cheapest

title: Compare servers side by side
